teaching_language: Fully English-taught. The programme is a stand-alone Italian second-cycle degree (laurea magistrale) of the Department of Management / School of Management and Economics, delivered entirely in English (it is not an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree, and it is not an interuniversity/joint degree). The official UNITO key-information sheet states: 'Language: English'. The second year splits into two majors (Finance & Accounting; Business Management & International Marketing), both taught in English.
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy - Department of Management / School of Management and Economics (SME), Corso Unione Sovietica 218 bis campus
degree_class: LM-77 (Scienze economico-aziendali / Management). UNITO internal course code: 1107M22. Apply@UniTo course id: 366.
admission_type: Restricted access (local numerus clausus - 'course with a local restricted number of places'). Admission is by a written admission test organised by the Department of Management, with an alternative route for holders of a GMAT or GRE certificate. Two independent test sessions per cycle, each producing its own ranking list; places are split 80% to the first session and 20% to the second session. [uncertain: the exact total number of places and the size of the non-EU (cat. 989) and Marco Polo (cat. 988) reserved quotas could not be read from the official pages, which were unreachable/Cloudflare-blocked]
application_deadline_eu: A.y. 2026/2027: candidates holding an Italian qualification apply through MyUniTO ('Enrolment > Pre-enrolment to courses with a restricted number of places') for one of the two test sessions - test dates 2 April 2026 (first session) and 16 September 2026 (second session). Candidates holding a FOREIGN qualification must first submit an Apply@UniTo application: 1st admission call 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026 (open to all applicants for postgraduate programmes, and the deadline that gives access to the 2 April 2026 test session); 3rd admission call 1 July - 14 September 2026 for restricted-number programmes, reserved to Italians, EU and EU-equivalent applicants and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy (this is the route to the 16 September 2026 session). [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU applicants residing abroad who need a visa (category 989): must apply on Apply@UniTo within the 1st admission call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026, in order to be admitted to the 2 April 2026 admission test; the later (3rd) call of 1 July - 14 September 2026 is expressly reserved to Italians, EU/EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy, so it is not available to visa applicants. Visa applicants must additionally submit the pre-enrolment application on Universitaly by 15 July 2026. Exception stated by the programme: non-EU candidates residing abroad who hold an ITALIAN first-cycle degree must not apply through Apply@UniTo but must contact internationaldegrees.management@unito.it. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: Written admission test (entry test for the Master's degree programmes of the Department of Management). Format: 30 multiple-choice questions on specific subjects, four options with one correct answer, 40 minutes. A published syllabus for the English version of the test lists the basic-knowledge topics. Two independent sessions for a.y. 2026/2027: 2 April 2026 and 16 September 2026, each generating a separate ranking. Alternative to sitting the test: submitting a valid GMAT or GRE certificate (obtained from 2018 onwards) in the attachments section of the application. Applicants scoring below the minimum threshold set in the official Call are marked 'Rejected'. No interview is mentioned. Indicative first-session calendar: provisional rankings by 30 April 2026, final rankings by 24 July 2026, enrolment window for admitted candidates 28-30 July 2026; second-session calendar: provisional rankings by 25 September 2026, final rankings by 23 October 2026.
academic_requirements: 1) A first-cycle (bachelor's) degree or an equivalent foreign first-cycle academic qualification is required; candidates may also apply while still completing the bachelor's ('graduated or about to graduate'). 2) Curricular requirement - for holders of a foreign qualification the requirement is considered fulfilled if the bachelor's is in Business Administration or Economics AND is from a university ranked in the top 100 of the Shanghai ranking for the Management area and/or from an institution ranked within the top 12.5% of the RePEc ranking of Economics departments. 3) Alternative curricular route: holding a GMAT or GRE certification obtained from 2018 onwards. 4) The general Department of Management rule for the Master's entry test states the curricular requirement is met with a bachelor's containing 48 ECTS/CFU in Business Administration, Economics, Law, Mathematics and Statistics (this is the department-wide wording; the Business Administration microsite states the ranking/GMAT-GRE variant for foreign qualifications). 5) In addition to the curricular requirement, candidates must pass the verification of adequate personal preparation (the admission test). A minimum overall score threshold applies (department-level documentation cites a minimum of 26/44 for the adequate-personal-preparation requirement in earlier cycles). 6) Numerus clausus: places are capped; 80% of places are assigned in the first session and 20% in the second. Applicant categories handled by the call: Italians, EU citizens and equivalents wherever resident, and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy (category 990); non-EU citizens residing abroad requiring a visa (category 989); Chinese students of the 'Marco Polo' Project (category 988), with reserved seats for categories 989 and 988. [uncertain: exact total places, exact non-EU reserved quota, and the exact 2026/2027 minimum score threshold]
language_requirements: English is the language of instruction and the admission test itself is sat in English. The official sources consulted do not state a mandatory English certificate on the programme's own admission-requirements page; UNITO's general rule is that 'whether you need an English/Italian certificate depends on the degree program you have chosen - in some cases an English certificate and a score can be specifically requested, in others the language knowledge will be verified during an interview or a test', with the programme-specific level shown in the 'Language requirements' section of the Apply@UniTo course page. A search-engine reading of the Apply@UniTo course page (course 366) reported a required English level of B1 or higher (CEFR); this could not be confirmed against the live page because apply.unito.it returns HTTP 403 to automated access. No Italian language certificate is required for this English-taught master (the B2 Italian certificate rule applies to Italian-taught programmes for non-EU applicants residing abroad). Applicants should treat the Apply@UniTo 'Language requirements' box for course 366 as the binding statement. [uncertain]
required_documents: For candidates with a foreign qualification applying through Apply@UniTo: complete online application (incomplete applications are not considered); first-cycle/bachelor's degree certificate or enrolment/near-graduation evidence; official transcript of records issued by the university, signed and sealed; upper-secondary qualification documentation where requested; documents accepted in Italian, English, French or Spanish, otherwise a certified translation into one of these languages; proof of authenticity/verification of the study documents (legalisation, Apostille, or a Statement of Verification issued by an ENIC-NARIC centre; the University may additionally request a Declaration of Value or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability/Verification); GMAT or GRE certificate (uploaded in the attachments section) if using that route instead of the admission test; English language certificate where the Apply@UniTo 'Language requirements' section requires one; identity document/passport. For candidates with an Italian qualification: application for the admission test submitted via MyUniTO with UNITO SCU credentials, followed by printing the admission-test application containing the pre-registration number. Visa applicants must also complete the Universitaly pre-enrolment. [uncertain: the full itemised document checklist is programme- and education-system-specific and is shown inside the Apply@UniTo application, which could not be read directly]

SPECIFIC UNCERTAINTIES:
1) English language requirement: the programme's own admission page does not appear to impose an English certificate, and one reading of the Apply@UniTo course-366 page reported 'English language knowledge is required at a B1 level or higher (CEFR)', while another reading stated that no English certificate is required. This conflict is unresolved - check the 'Language requirements' box on https://apply.unito.it/en_GB/courses/course/366-business-administration.
2) Number of places: only the 80%/20% split between the two sessions is documented; the absolute number of places and the reserved quotas for cat. 989 (non-EU abroad) and cat. 988 (Marco Polo) are published only in the 'Regulations for admission to the Master's degree programs a.y. 2026-2027' PDF, which could not be retrieved.
3) Curricular requirement wording: the programme microsite states the Shanghai top-100 / RePEc top-12.5% rule (apparently for foreign qualifications) plus the GMAT/GRE alternative, while the department-wide SME entry-test rules cite a '48 ECTS in Business Administration, Economics, Law, Mathematics, Statistics' requirement. It is unclear which applies to which applicant category for 2026/2027.
4) Deadlines: the Apply@UniTo call dates (25 Nov 2025 - 29 Jan 2026; 19 Feb - 15 Apr 2026; 1 Jul - 14 Sep 2026) are the university-wide calendar; the mapping of the 2nd call to this specific postgraduate programme was not confirmed (one source says the 2nd call is for undergraduate/single-cycle programmes only). The programme itself only names 29 January 2026 as the Apply@UniTo deadline for the April test session.
5) Minimum admission score: a 26/44 threshold appears in department-level documentation from an earlier cycle; the 2026/2027 threshold was not verified.
6) Naming ambiguity: a presentation PDF on the microsite is titled 'MASTER IN BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION - MBA (LM-77, 2-YEAR POSTGRADUATE DEGREE)'. This is the LM-77 laurea magistrale [1107M22], not a professional Level-1/Level-2 'Master' course. UNITO separately lists an unrelated professional master [M11128] also called 'Business Administration' - do not confuse the two.
7) There are several similarly named UNITO programmes (Business Administration and Control [1102M21], Business & Management [Apply id 564], Amministrazione aziendale [570], Amministrazione e controllo aziendale [369]); the item researched here is unambiguously Apply@UniTo course 366 / UNITO code 1107M22 / microsite business-administration.unito.it.
8) Enrolment window '28-30 July 2026' for admitted first-session candidates was reported by a single reading and may be approximate.
